correctness.rationale: Every phase normalization is explicit. Subtraction of Euler node updates gives the exact two-dimensional torus map and the center/transverse formulas. For 0<h<2/3, transverse multiplier absolute value is less than one, a small invariant rectangle exists, and the center factor stays positive; its ratio to transverse differences yields exponentially small transverse contamination. Taylor expansion of sin u(cos u−1) gives center factor 1−hu²/2+hu⁴/8+O(u⁶); exact reciprocal-square expansion and a summable remainder prove Y_n=hn+(3h−1)log(n)/4+C+o(1). Independently, for 0<h<1/3 the weighted Laplacian has spectrum 0,2,3, so the discrete gradient map is a global torus diffeomorphism with strict Lyapunov descent; all iterates converge to one of four stationary classes. The source, two hyperbolic saddles and local parabolic sink are correctly classified, so the sink basin has full Haar measure. The invariant equality-of-outer-phases circle is exactly the full exponentially convergent set in that basin. The actual bundled script verified 279 finite identities/trajectories and 12 exact rational coefficients; its finite outputs are not the proof of infinite conclusions.

value.rationale: At the exact isosceles frustration boundary, ordinary linear stability has a marginal eigenvalue and fails to determine the relaxation of three interacting phases. The concrete result completely separates exceptional exponential synchronization from typical critical inverse-square relaxation, gives full-measure global convergence for the natural diffeomorphic step range, and computes a physically interpretable step-dependent logarithmic correction, including its exact sign-changing threshold. This is a motivated complete critical-rate classification of the smallest frustrated triangle, not a random parameter slice; it supplies quantitative transient scales and distinguishes the discrete map from its ODE analogue. General normal-form tools are acknowledged and the global claim is strictly limited to 0<h<1/3.
